subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Find the eccentricity, coordinates of foci of the ellipse 3x² + y² − 6x − 2y − 5 = 0.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Senior Inter Maths-2B (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.58 — SAQ chapter 8 Ellipse, answer 61, on a ★★★ SSP page (book p.49 chapter table). Printed appearance: AP 15 only — no TS tag printed. Book p.58 prints NO margin mark tags for this question, so the 2+1+1 split is OURS: only two results are asked here (eccentricity, foci — no directrices, no latus rectum), so this card gives more weight (2 marks) to the completing-the-square step, which is the larger share of the work when only two short final results follow it. This ellipse is VERTICAL (a < b), same as Q60. Ellipse is an SAQ-ONLY unit on the book's IPE Blue Print (book p.5). No two-book union check and no board back-test were possible for Maths-2B (no second-year TSBIE BLM on hand; the book's five Guess Papers pp.118-127 are the orchestrator's back-test stand-in). The book writes the intermediate eccentricity step as √(6/9) = √6/9 = √2/3, where the middle term drops the radical over the whole fraction — the final value √2/3 (meaning √(2/3), not (√2)/3) is numerically correct and this card writes it with the radical placed unambiguously over the whole fraction throughout. insider_note: Only two results are asked here, not four, so half of the four marks are actually earned in the completing-the-square step — get the centre (1, 1) right and the rest follows quickly.

steps.label: Standard form
steps.margin_note: First two marks. Group the x-terms and y-terms, then complete each square.
steps.memory_tip: Divide by the number on the right at the very end.
steps.why: Completing the square in both x and y gives the shifted standard form, from which a², b² and the centre (h, k) can be read directly.
common_mistakes: Adding 1 and 1 inside the brackets but forgetting the 3× multiplier when adding to the right-hand side.
Reading the centre as (−1, −1) instead of (1, 1) — the sign inside (x − h)² is opposite to h.

steps.label: Eccentricity
steps.margin_note: Third mark. a² = 3, b² = 9, so a < b — the ellipse is vertical.
steps.memory_tip: Vertical ellipse: use b² − a² over b², under one square root.
lines: Since a < b, the ellipse is vertical.
steps.why: For a vertical ellipse the eccentricity formula uses b² − a² over b², all under one square root — the fraction is simplified only after the whole thing is under the root.
common_mistakes: Taking the square root of the numerator and denominator separately and losing track of which one is under the root.
Using a² − b² instead of b² − a² for a vertical ellipse, which gives a negative value.

steps.label: Foci
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. Foci move along y = k ± be from the shifted centre (1, 1).
steps.memory_tip: be = b times e — multiply the two numbers found above.
steps.why: The b and the 3 in be cancel neatly here, since b = 3 and e has a 3 in its denominator — always simplify be before writing the final coordinates.
common_mistakes: Leaving be unsimplified as 3·√6/3 instead of cancelling to √6.
Writing the foci as (1 ± be, 1), which puts them on the wrong axis for a vertical ellipse.
